pageLayout.accountAvatar: Shared 32px circular Avatar uses the personal identity image, with initials during loading or failure and no-referrer requests. Account name remains the accessible identity.
pageLayout.alignment: All workspace destinations share one full-width page grid. Team and hosted Billing embed inside AppShell's shared Settings Page, below its text-only route navigation, without another page heading. The admin Organization name panel sits above the existing Members card with the same management-panel padding. Prose and individual form rows carry their own readable measure.

teamAlignment.reservedActionColumn: Every row, including read-only and Pending rows, reserves the action column.
teamAlignment.roleAlignment: Read-only role text aligns with native select text; the Pending badge starts in the same role column.
teamAlignment.compactRows: At management-container widths of 600px and below, every role and action moves beneath its identity, with 12px row padding, a 4px identity-to-role gap and 44px interactive targets.
teamAlignment.contentMeasure: Roster and row separators fill the card; organization and invitation form rows use the existing 640px form measure.
teamAlignment.identityAndLabels: Show plain You text beside the current member name; invitations use the shared Field with a visible Email address label.
teamAlignment.forms: Organization-name and invitation forms share oc-management-form and the existing form measure so input and button boundaries align.
teamAlignment.compactForms: At container widths of 400px and below, both forms stack identically.

narrative.overview:
Night is the getopencrawl.com identity: a plain black canvas, near-black surfaces
with hairline boundaries, Geist type, and periwinkle actions drawn from the
OpenCrawl mark. The console applies that identity to compact, readable operational
work. Hierarchy comes from type, spacing, rows and sections; color identifies
interaction and meaningful status.

Core owns the shared visual system for hosted and single-tenant deployments.
`web/tokens.css` remains the canonical palette, fonts, spacing, radii and elevation
source. `web-v2/src/design/tokens.css` extends it with console dimensions and focus
constants; `web-v2/src/design/styles.css` owns the React layout and component
presentation. The frontmatter records their approved values; update the owning
CSS and this document together. Color aliases are resolved here without changing
the source color format. The sidecar carries motion, depth and component previews.

The retained `web/frame.css` and `web/controls.css` describe the earlier shared
frame and controls; they do not own the React workspace shell. React onboarding
preserves its approved presentation in `web-v2/src/onboarding/onboarding.css`.
Use the existing self-hosted fonts, OC marks, provider logos and shared SVG icons.
The font license remains at `web/assets/Geist-OFL.txt`.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-only Night palette and inherited brand assets.
One React workspace shell, with compact rows and a persistent desktop sidebar.
Quiet default controls, visible keyboard focus and explicit operational states.
A separate focused onboarding composition within the same design system.

rules.name: The Shared Palette Rule
rules.body:
Feature pages use the canonical Night tokens; a new
reusable visual value belongs in the core design system, never a page-local palette.

rules.name: The One Shell Rule
rules.body:
Pages own their content; core owns workspace navigation,
responsive chrome and shared layout. Internal links use the router and preserve
history without document reloads. Full navigation is for external authorization,
authentication and deployment boundaries.

rules.name: The Workspace Page Rule
rules.body: Workspace routes compose Page and PageHeader on one 1200px full-width grid, with stable title position, 8px description gap and 32px body gap. Bound form rows to 640px with oc-form-measure.

rules.name: The Identity Color Rule
rules.body: Use shared identity classes on board author names; never treat color as status, authorization, or a unique identifier.

dos: Do reuse the Night tokens, existing brand assets and self-hosted Geist fonts.
Do compose each workspace page from the shared shell, layout and controls.
Do show labeled loading, empty, error, busy and current states with recovery.
Do preserve the approved onboarding composition, receipts and optional invitations.
Do verify keyboard focus, narrow layouts, internal history and onboarding appearance.
donts: Don't create another workspace navigation, page-local palette or feature stylesheet.
Don't substitute new illustrations, fonts or provider marks for the inherited assets.
Don't use status color without explanatory text or make client visibility an authority check.
Don't replace onboarding's focused panel with the console sidebar or change its gates for styling.
